_comment: Third-party charts the platform installs, pinned to an exact version and
installed in this order by scripts/cluster-up.mjs. Nothing is installed from
an unpinned `helm install` in a script or a README, so the rehearsal cluster
and the graded demo get identical components.
targets: the clusters a chart goes on, kind (the rehearsal cluster) and eks
(the demo platform, D-093). values is read on both; eksValues is laid over it
on EKS. set names values read from terraform/platform's outputs at install
time (value path: output name), because they change with every AWS day.
stage secrets: installed before everything else on EKS, because the charts
after it read Secrets it makes (k8s/eks/secrets).
kube-prometheus-stack comes before the rest: its CRDs (ServiceMonitor,
PrometheusRule) must exist before any other chart or manifest declares one.

charts.why: Turns splitx/demo/* in AWS Secrets Manager into the same Kubernetes Secrets k8s:up builds from .env on Kind, so the other charts and the app read them unchanged. Nothing on EKS generates a secret.
Prometheus, Alertmanager and Grafana, run by the Prometheus Operator, with kube-state-metrics and node-exporter for what Kubernetes and the nodes are doing.
Turns the Ingresses into one Application Load Balancer, which admits only CloudFront, with the pods as its targets. Replaces ingress-nginx on EKS.
Turns Ingress objects into a real HTTP entry point on 80/443.
Supplies the CPU readings the HorizontalPodAutoscaler scales on. EKS runs it as a managed add-on (terraform/platform/cluster.tf).
Adds the fourth node when pods can't be placed on three, and removes it when it is no longer needed.
Stores the logs of the pods, searchable in Grafana by label and by request ID.
Reads the application and ingress logs through the Kubernetes API, parses their JSON, and sends them to Loki.
Refuses, at admission, any image from our registry that the release workflow did not sign. Installed before Jenkins so the policy is in force before anything can deploy.
Deploys releases GitHub Actions signed, when GitHub announces them, and rolls back what does not come up healthy. Its first start downloads its pinned plugins, hence the longer wait.
